newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe jumps after takeover rumours.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe jumps after takeover rumours.

text.p: Shares of CompuServe Inc jumped on Tuesday after a report was issued by Wall Street Strategies which said that the company is rumored to be in talks to be acquired by its rival America Online Inc.

"We got a rumor from a pretty good source that a deal is in the works," said Charles Payne, president and chief analyst at Wall Street Strategies, an investment research firm. "We think that when the smoke clears, you will have Microsoft and AOL as the only two providers of online services."
CompuServe shares closed up 1-09/16 to 11. Neither CompuServe nor AOL officials could be reached for comment.
Payne said he has been recommending investors buy AOL and he now is recommending CompuServe. He said any deal would have to be a stock transaction.

"The stock was trading at $9 and it has a book value of $7.50," Payne said. "Just from the risk reward level it was intriguing to begin with....The main drawback is the price, we are talking about a deal over $1 billion. There would not be a lot of premium in the deal," adding that he estimates a deal for CompuServe at about $14 to $15 a share.
